messages:
Devon: Heads-up — saw a spike in spot evictions in us-west1 this morning. Want to lock down an ops playbook for mixed-capacity pools.
Maya: agreed. saw a bump in Preemptible % at ~05:07, jobs requeued. stack traces look like normal eviction.
Sam: did autoscaler handle fallback to on-demand? any throttling?
Devon: autoscaler did kick but slow; we hit cooldown because of surge. some long-running training pods lost checkpoints.
Anika: can we define an explicit drain procedure for spot nodes so stateful jobs have a faster path to checkpoint?
Maya: yes — propose: 1) detect eviction 2) cordon node 3) annotate pods with evacuation timestamp 4) trigger fsync/flush hook for training jobs 5) prefer restart on dedicated/on-demand pool.
Devon: draft playbook snippet below (short):
```
# on eviction event
kubectl cordon <NODE>
kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<NODE> -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl annotate {} ops/evac-start="$(date -u +%s)"
# signal app-level checkpoint
kubectl exec <POD> -- /app/checkpoint --reason=eviction || echo "no checkpoint hook"
# graceful drain, ignore daemonsets
kubectl drain <NODE> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
Sam: add a preemptible-specific pod disruption budget fallback to force quick restarts on on-demand pools?
Maya: yes, PDBs should be tuned low for spot workloads. set maxUnavailable=1 for batch GPU jobs.
Anika: escalation path idea: if eviction rate > 3% in 30m AND fallback to on-demand fails, auto-open incident (ops-oncall) and reduce spot percentage in mixed pool by 20%.
Devon: +1. we can implement an autoscaler policy: when eviction_rate > threshold => scale down spot target and scale up on-demand target. keep total capacity stable.
Maya: monitoring checklist for the runbook: GPU eviction metric, kube pod restarts, queue backlog (jobs waiting), node provisioning time for on-demand, cost delta.
Riley-bot: Incident alert triggered when: gpu_spot_evictions[30m] > 3% AND on_demand_provision_time > 3m. Posting to #eng-oncall. :rotating_light:
Sam: we should include quick commands for manual mitigation in runbook, e.g.:
```
# reduce spot allocation
terragrunt apply -var='spot_target_percent=30' -auto-approve
# or on GCP
gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling <IG> --max-num-replicas=<N>
```
Anika: document app-level hooks: training code should listen for SIGTERM and call checkpoint, or expose /checkpoint endpoint. Put a 90s grace-period in runtime config.
Devon: ops-runbook section for who to call: 1) page eng-oncall via PagerDuty (ops-oncall) 2) if provisioning in a cloud region, cc cloud infra lead (Maya) 3) if cost impact > $X/day, finance-notify (via ops-tickets).
Maya: also note region constraints: some zones in eu-west have very low spot pool diversity; prefer us-west/central for non-sensitive workloads.
Sam: quick note on cost: fallback to on-demand increases cost — autoscaler policy should prefer short-lived burst nodes (if supported) instead of full on-demand long-lived.
Anika: include a post-incident checklist: collect eviction timelines, pod checkpoint success rates, restart locations, cost delta, and a follow-up TODO to raise spot percentage if supply stabilizes.
Devon: can someone add a one-pager to the repo and a short Slack snippet for on-call? I can convert this thread into a PR.
Maya: I’ll draft the PDB and grace-period defaults. Sam — can you add metrics and alert rules to prometheus?
Sam: on it. will add gpu_spot_evictions, pod_eviction_latency, on_demand_provision_time.
Riley-bot: Saved draft playbook to /ops/runbooks/spot-mixed-pool-eviction.md (draft). :white_check_mark:
Anika: thanks. adding a reminder: test this during low-traffic window — run a simulated eviction to ensure hooks work.
Devon: nice. tagging follow-ups: @Maya (PDBs), @Sam (alerts), @Anika (app hooks), I’ll open the PR and link here.
incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0457 (eviction-surge-us-west). Ops oncall paged.
Maya: final quick tip for runbook: keep node-labels consistent (pool=spot/dedicated), use taints + tolerations to control which pods can land on reclaimed nodes.
Devon: perfect. closing the thread once PR exists. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
